answer: The rope ferry is pulled hand over hand across the river and the ferry master measures the rope's wear after every crossing, logging the fray in his book. A zenith crossing made on a fresh rope fails the counter: at the tide of the rope the wear must match the crossings the master logged, and a fresh rope shows no wear at all. Faking the crossings means pulling the ferry for a season, wearing out three ropes and paying 7,900, while the nadir entry in the master's book is checked against the toll box, so a crossing whose wear was never measured is refused at the far bank.
